assumptions: Limit orders constitute roughly 35% of total order placement traffic, explaining why error rate plateaued at ~35% while other order types succeeded.
args.executive_summary: Starting at 10:11 UTC on 2026-03-10, orders-service experienced an error rate surge from 0.3% to approximately 35%, causing api-gateway error rate to rise to 8.8% and customer order placements to fail with HTTP 500. The incident was triggered by deployment dep-0009 (orders-service 4.18.0), which refactored limit-price validation and rolled out between 10:08 and 10:12 UTC. Orders-service logs show 600 occurrences of NullPointerException in LimitPriceValidator.validate starting immediately at 10:11 UTC. Downstream dependencies including orders-db, quotes-service, and risk-service remained completely healthy. Rolling back orders-service to version 4.17.3 immediately mitigates the issue.

facts.text: Deployment dep-0009 rolled out orders-service version 4.18.0 (from 4.17.3) between 10:08:00Z and 10:12:00Z with the summary 'Refactor limit-price validation; switch to the new quote client'.
The error rate of orders-service surged from a baseline mean of 0.29% to 34.69% starting at 10:11:00Z.
The error rate of api-gateway increased from 0.30% to 8.81% starting at 10:11:00Z.
Median request latency on orders-service dropped from 45.23ms to 29.82ms at 10:11:00Z.
Orders-service logged 600 instances of NullPointerException in LimitPriceValidator.validate between 10:11:00Z and 10:30:59Z, with zero prior occurrences.
Orders-service logged 600 instances of 'Order failed: internal error (500)' between 10:11:02Z and 10:30:59Z.
Api-gateway logged 400 instances of 'Upstream orders-service returned 500 for POST /api/v1/orders' starting at 10:11:06Z.
Order request throughput remained constant at approximately 120 rps before and during the incident.
Orders-service database pool wait time and risk check latency remained stable at 2.0ms and 20.1ms respectively throughout the window.
Quotes-service error rate stayed normal at approximately 0.20% with zero error logs throughout the window.
The drop in orders-service median latency resulted from limit orders failing fast in validation before reaching downstream database or risk service operations.
The ~35% failure rate in orders-service directly matches the fraction of incoming orders subjected to limit-price validation.
